question: Which statement best describes Two directories, two systems?
options: In the App Router every component is a React Server Component unless you add 'use client'. Server Components run only on the server, never ship their JS to the browser, and can fetch data directly. The Pages Router has no Server Components — its components are client components that hydrate fully, even when only displaying static data.

The App Router introduces layout.tsx files that wrap a route segment and all its children, and crucially persist across navigation without re-rendering. Layouts nest, so you can compose a root layout, a section layout, and a page. The Pages Router has only a single global _app.tsx and manual layout patterns, with no built-in nested, persistent layouts.

The Pages Router lives in pages/ and the App Router lives in app/. They can even coexist in one project. The App Router (default and recommended since Next 13/14) is built on React Server Components and modern data fetching; the Pages Router is the original, client-component-based system that still works for legacy apps.

The App Router adds special files: loading.tsx automatically shows a fallback (via React Suspense) while a segment loads, and error.tsx (a Client Component) catches errors in that segment and renders a fallback UI. The Pages Router has none of these conventions — you wire up loading and error states manually in each page.

The Pages Router has no Server Components — its components are client components that hydrate fully, even when only displaying static data.

The Pages Router fetches data with exported functions: getServerSideProps (per request, SSR), getStaticProps (build time, SSG), and getStaticPaths (dynamic static routes). The App Router replaces all of these: you simply make the Server Component async and await fetch, and the rendering mode (SSG/ISR/SSR) follows the fetch's caching options.

question: Which statement best describes Nested layouts?
options: Use the App Router for all new projects: it has Server Components, nested layouts, streaming, and is where Next.js development is focused. Stay on (or keep) the Pages Router only for existing apps that are not yet migrated, or when a dependency hasn't caught up to Server Components. They can run side by side during a transition.

options: Use the App Router for all new projects: it has Server Components, nested layouts, streaming, and is where Next.js development is focused. Migration is incremental: app/ and pages/ coexist, so you move routes one at a time. Convert getStaticProps to a cached async fetch, getServerSideProps to a no-store fetch or force-dynamic, _app/_document to root layout.tsx, and add 'use client' to components that use hooks, browser APIs, or event handlers. Move data fetching down into the components that need it.
